ga_half_pipe_area_2.blurb: Half Pipe Area is a pure bouldering zone inside the Boat Rock boulderfield in southwest Atlanta, one of several sub-sections there. It holds 13 problems on sharp granite, mostly slabby with the odd arete. Grades run from the very easy end of the scale up through V4 for the bulk of the problems, with a short tail of harder lines reaching into the high V-grades. Because the lower grades are plentiful it works for a mixed group, though several of the stronger problems keep it from being a beginner-only stop. The elevation is modest, around 900 feet, and the boulders sit in a neighbourhood setting rather than deep woods.

ga_soviet_cave_area.blurb: Soviet Cave Area is a small bouldering pocket in the Palisades section of the Atlanta metro. The centrepiece is a large cave sitting above a swampy flat, which gives pumpy traverses and the chance of a long roof link-up. Thirteen problems are listed, from a bare-bones warm-up to a hard open project in the V8 to V9 range, though most of the climbing falls between about V0 and V2 with a few steeper lines in the middle grades. Expect to bring a couple of crash pads and a spotter to shuffle them along the cave floor. Sun reaches the wall late in the day and summer leaf cover softens it.

ga_noon_wall.blurb: Noon Wall, also known locally as The Barrelhouse, is a bouldering wall tucked up the hillside above the river in the Buford Dam boulder collection. It gets its name from the sun reaching the face around midday, leaving it bright. The wall holds 12 problems with a wide spread: a few easy-to-moderate lines around V1 to V3, a solid middle band of V3 to V5, and a handful of serious hard problems running into the V10 and V11 range. The walk in is flat but long, roughly half an hour along the riverbank past the other boulders, so it suits a committed session more than a quick stop.

ga_asphalt_boulders.blurb: The Asphalt Boulders are a compact cluster of 12 problems in the Middle Maze of Rocktown, the sandstone bouldering field in northwest Georgia. They sit only a few feet from a neighbouring warm-up boulder, so a session can move easily between easy and harder lines. The grades cover a broad range: a few V0 to V2 problems, a middle group at V3 to V5, and some firm V6 and V7 lines. The problems are well liked, with even the easiest carrying star ratings, which makes this a good place to spend an hour or two when the rest of the maze is busy.
